title: Appraisal Orders Held by One Borrower
content:
**Appraisal Order — number of orders a borrower may hold.**

A customer may have any number of Appraisal Orders, across loan files and over time; there is no limit per customer. Each Appraisal Order belongs to exactly one Mortgage Loan File. Orders on the same loan file are read together under the rule on orders per loan file.

| Question | Answer under this rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a cap on how many Appraisal Orders one borrower may have? | No. The number per customer is unlimited. |
| Can one Appraisal Order support two loan files? | No. Each order belongs to exactly one loan file. |
| How are several orders on one loan file read? | Together, under the rule on orders per loan file. |

*Hypothetical illustration:* a borrower with a purchase file this year and a refinance file on another home may hold an Appraisal Order on each file; the two orders are separate, each tied to its own file, and the borrower's count of orders is not limited.
